narrative_purpose: Grounds the detection section in our own point of view: an observatory on Earth pointed at the single brilliant star that is Alpha Centauri, the world we would actually search from.
subject: A large domed astronomical observatory perched on a dark mountain ridge at night, its dome slit open. Above it, a deep field of faint stars, and low near the horizon one single intensely brilliant star burning far brighter than the rest.
scene: A clear high-altitude night under a southern sky. The observatory silhouetted against the faint glow of the night horizon; the one brilliant star dominating the lower sky as the obvious target of the open dome.
camera: Wide low-angle landscape shot, the observatory on the ridge in the lower third, vast star-field sky above.
light: Night: the brilliant low star is the brightest point; faint cool ambient skyglow on the dome and ridge; deep shadow elsewhere.
palette: Void-indigo and deep-teal night sky, cool mist-grey on the dome and ridge, one scarce warm-white brilliant star, faint cyan airglow on the horizon.
style: Painterly naturalist nightscape plate, atmospheric, restrained - this is the one figure set on Earth, so keep it sober and real.
detail_level: Crisp silhouette of the dome and ridgeline; soft star-field; the brilliant star with a gentle painterly glow, not a lens flare.
composition: Observatory dome on the lower-right third; the single brilliant star low on the left horizon; broad dark sky filling the upper frame.
consistency_notes: This is the only Earth-set figure in the chapter; it deliberately drops the bioluminescent glow and keeps a sober night palette, while still using the cool void-indigo/teal sky of the book.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no logos, no lens flares, no photographic or 3D-render look, no oversaturation, no alien plants
